'''Marileen Dogterom''' (born 20 November 1967, in [[Utrecht]]) is a Dutch biophysicist and professor at the [[Kavli Institute of Nanoscience]] at [[Delft University of Technology]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tudelft.nl/tnw/over-faculteit/afdelingen/bionanoscience/research/research-labs/marileen-dogterom-lab/people/|title=People|website=TU Delft|language=nl|access-date=2018-06-29}}</ref> She is notable for her research of the cell [[cytoskeleton]]. She was awarded the 2018 [[Spinoza Prize]] for her research.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://www.nwo.nl/en/research-and-results/programmes/spinoza+prize/spinoza+laureates/overview+in+alphabetical+order/marileen+dogterom|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190322214441/https://www.nwo.nl/en/research-and-results/programmes/spinoza+prize/spinoza+laureates/overview+in+alphabetical+order/marileen+dogterom|title=Prof dr A.M. (Marileen) Dogterom|publisher=NWO|archive-date=22 March 2019}}</ref>

== Life and career ==
Dogterom was born 20 November 1967 in Utrecht, the Netherlands. In 1990, she earned a degree in theoretical physics from the [[University of Groningen]].<ref name=":0" /> Two years later, the [[Fulbright Program]] granted her a fellowship.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Dogterom_Marileen|title=Academy of Europe: Dogterom Marileen|last=Hoffmann|first=Ilire Hasani, Robert|website=www.ae-info.org|access-date=2018-06-29}}</ref> Though she found a PhD position at the [[University of Paris-Sud]], she followed her mentor ([[Stanislas Leibler]]) to [[Princeton University]], where Dogterom began to work with biological systems via a collaboration with their biology faculty.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=http://tu-delft.instantmagazine.com/tu-delft/portraits-2017#!/marileen-dogterom-interview-en|title=portraits 2017|website=tu-delft.instantmagazine.com|access-date=2018-06-29}}</ref> In 1994, she graduated cum laude with a doctorate from the [[University of Paris-Sud]],<ref name=":0" /> with a thesis on "Physical Aspects of Microtubule Growth and Mitotic Spindle Formation,"<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.academia-net.org/profil/prof-dr-marileen-dogterom/1163461|title=Prof. Dr. Marileen Dogterom - AcademiaNet|website=www.academia-net.org|language=en|access-date=2018-06-29|archive-date=2018-06-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180629130741/http://www.academia-net.org/profil/prof-dr-marileen-dogterom/1163461|url-status=dead}}</ref> and worked as a postdoc at [[Bell Labs]] in the [[United States]]. In 1997, she became a project leader at FOM Institute [[AMOLF]], a physics and biophysics research institute, becoming head of department from 2003 to 2013.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" />

Dogterom holds professional ties to various universities. In 2000, she became a professor at [[Leiden University]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/staffmembers/marileen-dogterom#tab-1|title=Marileen Dogterom|website=Leiden University|language=en-US|access-date=2018-06-29}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.medicaldelta.nl/network/professors/marileen-dogterom|title=Marileen Dogterom|website=www.medicaldelta.nl|language=en-US|access-date=2018-06-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180629074255/http://www.medicaldelta.nl/network/professors/marileen-dogterom|archive-date=2018-06-29|url-status=dead}}</ref> and become a full professor in 2010.<ref name=":0" /> She was the Chair of the Department of Bionanoscience at the Kavli Institute of Nanoscience at Delft University of Technology from 2014 to 2021.<ref name=":1" /> Since 2016, she has held the title of "Medical Delta Professor," meaning she held professorships at both Delft and Leiden.<ref name=":0" />

In 2006, Dogterom took a sabbatical for a year to work at [[Erasmus MC]] in [[Anna Akhmanova]]'s research group, which specialized in cell biology and cytoskeletons. In 2013, they received an ERC Synergy grant to collaborate on research on cytoskeleton regulation by the cell.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.uu.nl/en/news/71-meu-erc-synergy-grant-for-prof-anna-akhmanova-and-prof-marileen-dogterom|title=7,1 M€ ERC Synergy Grant for prof. Anna Akhmanova and prof. Marileen Dogterom|last=van der Garde|first=Monica|date=2014-12-15|work=Utrecht University|access-date=2018-06-29|language=en}}</ref>

[[File:Marileen Dogterom 2019.jpg|thumb|upright=0.7|Dogterom in 2019]]

Dogterom currently leads a team that aims to build the first [[artificial cell]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nwo.nl/en/research-and-results/programmes/spinoza+prize/spinoza+laureates/overview+in+alphabetical+order/marileen+dogterom/interview+pushing+and+pulling+inside+a+cell|title=Pushing and pulling inside a cell|last=Karolien|website=www.nwo.nl|language=en|access-date=2018-06-29|archive-date=2018-06-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180629050129/https://www.nwo.nl/en/research-and-results/programmes/spinoza+prize/spinoza+laureates/overview+in+alphabetical+order/marileen+dogterom/interview+pushing+and+pulling+inside+a+cell|url-status=dead}}</ref> In her laboratory, her team studies and builds parts of the cytoskeleton outside of the cell, where they can measure the forces they exert on various other cell components. The team also analyses the effects of various forces on the deformation of the cytoskeleton, the interactions of the cytoskeleton polymers as a network, and the spatial structure of the cell itself. Her research group plans to collaborate with various other research groups that focus on other parts of the cell.<ref name=":3" />

In 2018, Dogterom was awarded a [[Spinoza Prize]], which grants a large sum to a team conducting novel research in the Netherlands. Dogterom's former colleague [[Anna Akhmanova]] was awarded a Spinoza Prize in the same year.<ref name=":0" /> Dogterom served as Vice President of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] from 2020 to 2022,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/about-us/organisation/bestuur |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200920115938/https://www.knaw.nl/en/about-us/organisation/bestuur |title=Academy Board |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |archive-date=20 September 2020}}</ref> and as President from 2022 to 2026.<ref>{{cite web |title=KNAW Academy afternoon 2022 |url=https://www.knaw.nl/bijeenkomsten/akademiemiddag-2022 |website=KNAW}}</ref>

== Awards ==
In 2013, Dogterom was elected to the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] (EMBO),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://people.embo.org/profile/marileen-dogterom |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170826065126/https://people.embo.org/profile/marileen-dogterom |title=Marileen Dogterom |publisher=European Molecular Biology Organization |date= |archive-date=26 August 2017}}</ref> and in 2015, she was elected to the [[Academia Europaea]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /> She has been a member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] since 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/6130|title=Dogterom, Prof. dr. A.M. (Marileen) — KNAW|website=www.knaw.nl|language=en|access-date=2018-06-29|archive-date=2019-03-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190322214319/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/6130|url-status=dead}}</ref> Dogterom has been awarded the following grants, fellowships, and prizes:<ref name=":2" />

* 2025 - Professor of Excellence Award | Leermeesterprjis<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor of Excellence Award {{!}} Leermeesterprjis 2025 |url=https://www.tudelft.nl/en/tu-delft-teaching-academy/previous-newsletters/the-educator-september-2025/professor-of-excellence-award-leermeesterprjis-2025}}</ref>
* 2019 - Fellow of the [[Biophysical Society]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.biophysics.org/awards-funding/society-awards |title=Society Awards |publisher=Biophysical Society |date= |access-date=2026-07-31}}</ref>
* 2018 – [[Spinoza Prize]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nwo.nl/en/prof-dr-am-marileen-dogterom |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201106142101/https://www.nwo.nl/en/prof-dr-am-marileen-dogterom |title=Prof. dr. A.M. (Marileen) Dogterom |publisher=Netherlands Organisation for Scientific Research |date= |archive-date=6 November 2020}}</ref>
*2017 - Engineering and Physical Sciences [[Suffrage Science award]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Marileen Dogterom to receive a Suffrage Science award|url=https://www.tudelft.nl/en/2017/tnw/marileen-dogterom-to-receive-a-suffrage-science-award/|access-date=2021-05-13|website=TU Delft|language=en-US}}</ref>
* 2015 – Dutch Physical Prize (Yearly Award from the Dutch Physical Society)
* 2013 – ERC Synergy grant (with [[Anna Akhmanova]] at Utrecht University)
* 2007 – VICI Award, NWO Vernieuwingsimpuls
* 1992 – Fulbright Fellowship, The Netherlands
* 1991 – EMBO Short Term Fellowship (Heidelberg, Germany)
* 1988 – Fellowship from the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Rome, Italy)
